claims.statement: The deceased woman worked at the Irkutsk infectious-disease research institute.
The death of the laboratory worker was publicly reported.
Russian authorities publicly described the illness as pneumonia of unknown etiology or origin.
Pneumonic plague was established as the diagnosis.
claims.limit: WHO reports Russian testing did not identify plague among tested high-threat pathogens, while the fatal illness still lacks a confirmed causative agent.

claims.statement: The illness or death was established as linked to a pathogen handled at work.
Authorities reported that contacts were identified and monitored.
A dangerous infectious-disease pathogen was established among monitored contacts.
A second plague case was established.
claims.limit: A verification request or suspected-event report does not confirm a diagnosis or an additional death.

claims.statement: A second death connected to the suspected plague event was established.
claims.limit: A verification request or suspected-event report does not confirm a diagnosis or an additional death.

claims.statement: WHO published an initial, provisional risk assessment for this event.
The death resulted from occupational laboratory exposure.
claims.statement_zh: 死亡源于实验室职业暴露。
claims.limit: WHO states laboratory-associated exposure cannot be fully excluded; this does not establish that such exposure occurred.

claims.statement: WHO publicly stated that it requested additional information about the event.
claims.statement_zh: WHO 公开表述已索取本事件进一步信息。
claims.limit: Supports a verification procedure; it does not establish a pathogen diagnosis.

claims.statement: WHO requested verification of media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause.
claims.statement_zh: WHO 要求核实第二名员工病因未明肺炎的媒体说法。
claims.limit: A verification request does not confirm the reported second case.

claims.statement: The historical handoff records Reuters reporting that Russian regulators said about 90% of quarantined people had been released.
claims.statement_zh: 历史交接记录载有 Reuters 转述俄监管机构称约 90% 被隔离者已解除隔离；本轮未能重开该报道。
claims.limit: Retained historical attribution only; this article could not be reopened. Original release records and aligned population and time definitions are unavailable.

claims.statement: WHO reported that the Russian NFP said medical observation of all identified contacts had ended.
claims.statement_zh: WHO 转述俄罗斯 IHR 国家联络点称全部已识别接触者医学观察已经结束。
claims.limit: SUPPORTED only as an official WHO account of Russian NFP information. Underlying follow-up records remain unavailable, and WHO could not independently assess whether seven days excluded all plausible causes.

claims.statement: WHO had all necessary information and completed a fully informed risk assessment of this event.
claims.statement_zh: WHO 已获得完整信息并完成本事件充分公共卫生风险评估。
claims.limit: WHO issued a formal assessment but retained limited confidence: no confirmed etiology, insufficient basis to independently judge monitoring duration for all plausible causes, and laboratory-associated exposure not fully excluded.

claims.statement: WHO has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission associated with this event, based on information provided by the Russian NFP.
claims.statement_zh: 基于俄罗斯 IHR 国家联络点提供的信息，WHO 尚未识别出与本事件有关的持续传播证据。
claims.limit: No evidence identified is not proof that transmission was impossible. WHO states confidence is limited by the unconfirmed diagnosis and uncertain source and mode of exposure.

claims.statement: WHO stated that laboratory-associated exposure cannot be fully excluded at this stage.
claims.statement_zh: WHO 表示，现阶段仍不能完全排除实验室相关暴露。
claims.limit: This supports WHO’s uncertainty statement; it does not establish that a laboratory exposure occurred.

history.note: First public bounded review; no historical status was overwritten.
Recovered input mappings and read the WHO original statement. Initial and fully informed risk assessments are separate claims. Original v0.1 records remain unchanged.
UNOG source-date correction only; no clinical claim status changed. Previous snapshots and reviews remain immutable.
Two Russian press-service attributions retained in review as candidates. Clinical claims and accepted source records unchanged.
No new qualifying evidence. Clinical claims and accepted source records unchanged; official source access remains incomplete.
Accepted WHO DON620. Ongoing transmission evidence was not identified, but etiology, monitoring sufficiency and laboratory-exposure uncertainty remain.
No new qualifying evidence. WHO DON620 remains the latest accepted material evidence; clinical and evidence states unchanged.

sources.title: WHO statement carried by the United Nations Geneva newsroom
sources.publisher: United Nations Geneva / World Health Organization
sources.supports: A female laboratory worker died; authorities were testing the cause, monitoring identified contacts, and WHO published an initial risk assessment.
sources.does_not_establish: A causative agent, a diagnosis of pneumonic plague, an occupational pathogen link, a laboratory accident, a second plague case, or a second death.
sources.source_date_semantics: Date displayed on the UNOG newsroom article and its press-briefing dateline; original v0.1/v0.2 records preserved.

sources.title: WHO still did not know the causative agent in the Irkutsk death
sources.supports: WHO said it did not know the causative agent; the Russian public-health statement described pneumonia of unknown origin and reported testing of contacts.
sources.does_not_establish: That media speculation about plague or a laboratory accident is correct.

sources.title: Russian public-health statement reported no evidence tying the illness to worked-with pathogens
sources.supports: Russian authorities publicly reported pneumonia of unknown origin, no evidence of illness from pathogens handled at work, and no institute incident involving pathogenic microorganisms.
sources.does_not_establish: An independently replicated occupational-safety investigation or a final clinical diagnosis.

sources.title: Rospotrebnadzor commission findings reported by TASS
sources.supports: The cited commission reported no laboratory accident and used the diagnosis description pneumonia of unknown etiology.
sources.does_not_establish: Independent confirmation of the commission's methods or a final pathogen diagnosis.

sources.title: Fact check of circulating Irkutsk claims
sources.supports: The reviewed public record did not prove a laboratory accident; unrelated WHO and video material were circulating alongside the event.
sources.does_not_establish: A final diagnosis or an independent laboratory investigation.

sources.title: WHO plague fact sheet
sources.supports: Plague is a bacterial disease caused by Yersinia pestis and pneumonic plague has defined clinical and public-health characteristics.
sources.does_not_establish: That plague caused the Irkutsk worker's illness or death.
sources.source_date_semantics: Date displayed on the WHO page in this review; original publication date is not established.

sources.title: Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute public description
sources.supports: The institute publicly describes work on plague and other dangerous infectious diseases.
sources.does_not_establish: Which agent, if any, was involved in the worker's illness, or that a workplace incident occurred.

sources.title: WHO Director-General opening remarks, 7 October 2026
sources.supports: WHO sought laboratory-test information, reasons for public-health measures and contact health status; it sought verification of a second-employee media report and said the information was insufficient for a full risk assessment.
sources.does_not_establish: A plague diagnosis, an occupational exposure chain, a confirmed second case or a second death.

sources.title: Public post attributed to Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
sources.publisher: Named public LinkedIn account attributed to Tedros
sources.source_date_semantics: Only a relative 3h label was displayed; no absolute publication time was verified.
sources.supports: The post dates the reported death to 2 October and relays Russian information that medical observation of all identified contacts had ended.
sources.does_not_establish: Independently verified clinical or contact follow-up records, a confirmed pathogen, or that transmission has been excluded.

sources.title: Reuters follow-up retained from the recovered public handoff
sources.publisher: Reuters, attributing Russian regulators and WHO
sources.source_date_semantics: Historical handoff records 2026-10-07T09:06:00Z; not reverified during this review.
sources.supports: The historical public handoff records Reuters reporting an attributed claim that about 90% of quarantined people had been released.
sources.does_not_establish: Fresh access to the article, original release records, aligned contact populations and times, or exclusion of transmission.

sources.title: WHO Disease Outbreak News: pneumonia of undetermined etiology in the Russian Federation
sources.supports: WHO published that, based on Russian NFP information, it had not identified evidence of ongoing transmission; all identified contacts reportedly remained asymptomatic, tested negative for investigated high-threat pathogens and completed follow-up.
sources.does_not_establish: The causative agent, an independently verified complete contact record, sufficiency of the seven-day monitoring period for all plausible causes, or exclusion of a laboratory-associated exposure. WHO explicitly retained these uncertainties.
